test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year did Babur take control of Kabul?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1504 CE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, captured Kabul in **1504 CE**, marking a significant milestone in his career.
 
• At the time, Babur was only 21 years old and faced challenges due to his expulsion from his ancestral home in Ferghana (modern-day Uzbekistan).
 
• Taking control of Kabul provided Babur with a strategic base to consolidate his power and plan future expeditions into India.
 
• Kabul acted as a political and military center for Babur, enabling him to gather resources, troops, and allies for his campaigns.
 
• Babur’s conquest of Kabul was critical in his eventual establishment of the Mughal Empire in India after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 1500 CE**

 
 
• While Babur was active during this period, he was still struggling to establish his authority in Central Asia.
 
• He did not capture Kabul in 1500 CE but was involved in conflicts around Ferghana and Samarkand.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: 1508 CE**
 
 
• By 1508 CE, Babur had already consolidated his rule over Kabul and was planning further campaigns into northern India.
 
• During this time, Babur focused on strengthening his position in Afghanistan and surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 1512 CE**
 
 
• In 1512 CE, Babur attempted to regain control of Samarkand but was defeated by the Uzbeks under Muhammad Shaybani Khan.
 
• This event was significant in Babur’s life but unrelated to his conquest of Kabul, which had already occurred years earlier.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Babur’s Early Career**
 
 
• Babur was a descendant of Timur on his father’s side and Genghis Khan on his mother’s side, giving him a rich lineage of conquerors.
 
• His early career was marked by hardships, including losing his kingdom in Ferghana and struggling to regain political power.
 
• Capturing Kabul in 1504 CE was a turning point that allowed Babur to rebuild his fortunes and eventually pave the way for the establishment of the Mughal Empire.
